prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1351; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the left lane of northbound traffic on a Conroe, Texas roadway when Driver 2 failed to slow in time and struck the rear of the vehicle. Driver 1 was operating the vehicle at the time of impact, and a Passenger was also seated inside. Responding officers confirmed that Driver 1 and the Passenger were both present in the vehicle when the collision occurred, and that fact was consistent with statements taken at the scene. Driver 2 stated that the collision happened in the manner Driver 1 described, and two independent witnesses gave accounts that matched this description. Scene photographs were taken and reviewed. The damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle corresponds to the force and point of impact observed at the scene. No prior damage to the vehicle was reported or observed. Driver 1 reported neck and back discomfort following the impact, a complaint that fits the nature and force of a rear-end collision of this kind. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
